note: The npi not_null test's own description states the real table has 12,456,456 rows, but ~7,557 facilities (confirmed by the sibling health__fed_cms_dialysis roster mart) x a plausible ~50 measures x ~15 years only accounts for roughly 5-6M rows, and the SQL selects a MODALITY column (in-center HD / home HD / PD) that CMS dialysis quality measures are known to split on -- so modality is very likely a missing grain column the agent never checked, and ccn+measure_id+year alone would false-fail on legitimate same-measure-different-modality rows.

The SQL selects SUPLR_RENTL_IND (rental/purchase indicator), which is exactly the field the CMS DMEPOS-by-Supplier PUF uses to report the same supplier+HCPCS pair twice (once as a rental, once as a purchase), so the test's key of suplr_npi+hcpcs_cd would wrongly flag that legitimate rental-vs-purchase pair as a duplicate -- the indicator column needs to be in the key.

The claim that 'sibling 2023/2024 marts already test both id and establishment_id as unique' is false for 2023 -- schema_fed_osha_ita_300a_summary_2023.yml (same generator, same source family, checked directly) tests establishment_id not_null only, never unique -- which is real evidence within this repo that establishment_id can legitimately repeat within a filing year, so the added independent 'unique' test on establishment_id (on top of id) risks false-failing on legitimate repeats rather than catching a real load bug.

The chosen key is a verbatim copy of the batch file's hint columns and omits programme/leba_numtitle/eu_ref_num/date_file, which are also present in the SELECT and are exactly the fields that distinguish one EU-regulation listing from another -- a person re-sanctioned under a second regulation with identical entity/alias/address/ID/citizenship sub-records would collide on this key and read as a false duplicate.

The SQL wraps COUNTRY_CODE and COUNTERPART_AREA_CODE (and even COUNTRY_NAME/COUNTERPART_AREA_NAME) in try_to_number(), but World Bank IDS codes are alpha ISO-style strings (e.g. 'USA'), so those columns almost certainly evaluate to NULL for real data -- the test as coded then effectively tests uniqueness of (NULL, NULL, series_code), which will spuriously collide across every different country/counterpart-area sharing the same series_code; the agent's own reasoning flags this exact bug but ships the test on the broken columns anyway instead of routing around it or fixing the cast.

Ran the test live and it FAILS with 14,695 duplicate groups; root cause is the SQL's try_to_number(COUNTRY) and try_to_number(COUNTRY_SUBDIVISION_PRIMARY) casts, which turn every row's country/subdivision code (alphanumeric, e.g. 'US') into NULL, so the added key can never actually discriminate by geography despite naming those columns.

Ran the test live and it FAILS with 11,252 duplicate values; queried the underlying data directly and found oldcreativeid legitimately/literally repeats up to 185 times with the exact same newcreativeid each time (a genuine full-row duplication in the source), so single-column uniqueness on oldcreativeid is demonstrably false, not just a grain mismatch -- this is exactly the COUNT(DISTINCT)-before-trusting-a-key trap CLAUDE.md warns about.

Ran the test live and it fails; queried directly and found country, country_subdivision_primary, and country_subdivision_secondary are ALL NULL for every one of the 1,289 rows because of the same try_to_number() cast bug as advertiser_geo_spend, so the new schema file's key columns carry no real discriminating data at all.

Ran the added test live: it FAILS with 11,774 duplicate groups on 500,000 rows; adding the SQL's own pgm_sys_acrnm column to the key did not fix it, but testing against every column in the row showed only 1,493 true full-row duplicates exist -- meaning the remaining ~10,000+ failures are legitimate distinct records (differing in annual_emission/unit_of_measure/pgm_sys_acrnm) that this key incorrectly collapses together, the exact false-fail-on-legitimate-repeats trap the repo has hit before.

Ran the added test live and it FAILS with 498 duplicate groups; drilled into an example (pgm_sys_id=100000000000000031, activity_id=3601460207) and found 4 real rows differing only in activity_purpose_desc ('Core Program', 'Case Development', 'Applicability Determination', 'Citizen Complaint/Tip') and comp_monitor_type_code, meaning a single compliance activity legitimately serves multiple purposes and pgm_sys_id+activity_id alone is not the grain, contrary to the claimed 'EPA's own composite primary key' reasoning.

Live query shows the claimed 6-column key (indicator, c_group, state, subgroup, phase, time_period) has 72 real duplicate groups (612 rows): when phase='-1' the time_period field resets to '1' across many genuinely different survey windows (time_period_label shows 'July 22 - Aug 18, 2020' vs 'Nov 27, 2023 - Jan 8, 2024' etc. sharing the same key) -- adding time_period_label makes it perfectly unique (16,056/16,056), so the coverage-period label should have been in the key.
